title: In Silico Clinical Trials for Cardiovascular Disease
protocol: Log in to the SILICOFCM platform.
Choose the appropriate workflow for ultrasound image analysis using M-mode or Apical view.
Under Virtual Population Module, select ultrasound M-mode or Apical view workflow.
In the list of available workflows, choose the ultrasound-merged workflow.
Upload images and DICOM files from the local computer.
Visualize the created geometry of LV directly on the platform.
Select Shaded or Wireframe models for visualization.
Generate a mesh of finite elements based on extracted LV dimensions.
Run finite element analysis simulation with user-prescribed inlet and outlet velocities.
Use PAK finite element solver for fluid-structure simulations.
Apply Holzapfel model, hunter muscle model, or other built-in material models.
Input file is processed through the PAK preprocessor to output a DAT file.
DAT file serves as input for the finite element solver.
Solver outputs VTK files with simulation results including velocities, pressures, strains, and stresses in the left ventricle.
Download template files for inlet and outlet velocities using provided buttons.
Save downloaded template files into Private or Public folders.
Upload the saved files similar to how images are uploaded.
Modify default values for patient-specific conditions if available.
Click on the Execute button to start the workflow execution.
View ejection fraction and global work efficiency values by clicking the eye button.
Review diagrams of pressure vs. volume, pressure vs. strain, and myocardial work vs. time.
Download results folder containing VTK files, CSV files, and animations.
Click on the camera button to preview animations of displacement, pressure, shear stresses, and velocity fields.
Click on the 3D visualization button to visualize outputs online in ParaView Glance.
Load multiple VTK files previously downloaded as results.
Visualize several parameters of interest by changing the field, for example, to velocity.
Rotate the model or change the color scheme.
Choose Surface with edges or Wireframe for surface representation.
Apply the same methodology to every loaded VTK file.
Go to Execute Workflow and choose torse-cwl from available workflows.
Add a comment or note in the Comments section before executing.
Click on the Input Template File button and save content as input.txt file.
Select the downloaded input.txt file in the Input File field.
Import the selected file.
Click on the Execute button to start the calculation.
Wait for the workflow status to change from "running" to "finished ok".
Click on the eye or camera buttons to visualize simulation reports or animations.
Alternatively, click on the 3D visualization button to view outputs online in ParaView Glance.
Select the OPEN A FILE button and go to the GIRDER tab.
Enter user credentials if prompted.
Open the Private folder.
Select and open the workflow-outputs folder.
Open the torso-cwl folder.
Open the first folder on the list.
See the list of VTK files that represent the simulation results.
Choose one or more files and click on the SELECT button to load the file in ParaView Glance.
Manipulate the model geometry using the mouse (move, rotate, zoom).
Choose the Wireframe option to see the interior of the torso with a heart incorporated within the torso.
Choose the Points option to display a dotted representation of the torso model with full heart mesh.
Adjust the Point Size value to change the display results.
Adjust the Opacity value to see the interior of the torso and display results inside the heart mesh.
Click on the Color By drop-down menu and choose the desired option, for instance, electric potential.
Change the default color scale to any of the listed options.
